runs.gutSentence: Way better start, straight into the action. It's fast now, I died earlier than before but it felt like my fault.
The dash is nice, I can do the last second spin now and make them crash. Starting from wave 4 helps a lot.
themes: the dash and the last-second escape

runs.gutSentence: The decoy is cool, feels like a real trick. But I missed the dash, I kept pressing space.
themes: decoy as a new way to lure

runs.gutSentence: Getting there. Dash plus decoy is a good combo. The meta loop is better but I want more variety, more stuff to unlock.

pillarForecast.why: Collisions remain the core kill source; decoy and assist mines are player-placed or player-triggered, so kills still read as his idea.
B-level speed and density directly answer 'I want the high-octane moments'; wide turns keep it readable. Risk is a difficulty spike making early runs feel short.
Checkpoints change the starting wave, so 'run 5 vs run 1' is muddied; unlocks may get credited instead of skill.
Mines from wave 1, overlapping waves and the assist mine remove both 'slow to start' and 'lame with a single enemy'.
Charger is better telegraphed, but faster chasers plus denser waves will make chaser body-hits the dominant death, possibly in clutter he calls cheap.
Checkpoints and two unlocks help, but he asked for a changed meta loop; two unlocks may read as thin and he may ask for more.

biggestRisk: The faster, denser v2 opening punishes him earlier than v1 did (shorter first runs dying to chasers in clutter), so the first impression is 'harder' rather than 'more rush'; combined with a meta loop that still feels thin after the decoy, that could produce 'samey' again by run 8.
abVerdict: He prefers B (dash), about 65%. He'll express it by mentioning the dash positively in run 6 or 8 and noting he missed it in run 7, framed around pulling off the last-second escape; a minority chance he says the dash makes it too easy or doesn't notice much difference.
